Li, S., Zheng, H., Zheng, Y., Tian, J., Jing, T., Chang, J.-S. and Ho, S.-H. (2019). Recent advances in hydrogen production by thermo-catalytic conversion of biomass. International Journal of Hydrogen Energy 44(28), 14266-14278. doi:10.1016/j.ijhydene.2019.03.018

NO TECHNOLOGY PARAMETERS EXTRACTED. Review of laboratory research on hydrogen from biomass by fast pyrolysis/bio-oil reforming, gasification and catalytic (alkali, metal, carbonaceous, microwave-assisted) conversion: Table 1 is biomass ultimate/proximate analyses and Table 2 lists catalyst studies with hydrogen yields and conditions. It prints no process-scale energy use, efficiency, cost, capacity, emissions, capture or TRL - the same bar that put Ashik et al. 2015 in background. It does not support the IPCC AR6 Table 11.3 row it is cited for (850 degC woody biomass gasification with CCS, TRL 7-8, about USD 50-75/t): no TRL, cost or CCS appears; only the 800-850 degC autothermal reforming of bio-oil (Czernik et al.) loosely matches the temperature. What it has: Table 1 (p.14269): ultimate and proximate analyses of biomasses; Table 2 (p.14272-14273): catalytic biomass conversion studies (catalyst, temperature, hydrogen yield); bio-oil autothermal reforming at 800-850 degC raising the hydrogen yield to 9-11 g (basis split by the page break) (Czernik et al., p.14269); qualitative comparison of thermochemical, biological and electrolytic hydrogen routes.
This is the paper IPCC AR6 WGIII Ch.11 Table 11.3 footnote n cites as "Li et al. (2019)" (registered as li_2019_001).
